stemEn: Which Glasgow Coma Scale range is consistent with severe traumatic brain injury?
explanationAr: مفتاح المصدر B. يعرّف المصدر severe TBI بأنه GCS أقل من 9، بينما moderate هو 9–12 وmild هو 13–15.
clinicalPearl: Severe TBI in the source is GCS <9.

tts.text: Which Glasgow Coma Scale range is consistent with severe traumatic brain injury? Option A, nine to twelve. Option B, four to eight.

stemEn: A 10-year-old remains unresponsive after trauma and has a brief convulsion in the emergency department. What is the next investigation?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار Head CT؛ severe TBI يحتاج unenhanced head CT لتحديد النزف أو الآفات التي قد تتطلب تدخلًا عاجلًا.
clinicalPearl: Severe TBI requires prompt head CT after stabilization.

tts.text: A ten-year-old remains unresponsive after trauma and has a brief convulsion in the emergency department. What is the next investigation? Option A, head CT.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection, 4th Edition, 1 May 2026

stemEn: A child with traumatic brain injury has cerebral edema on CT. Which treatment is selected in the source?
explanationAr: مفتاح المصدر B: hypertonic 3% saline. شرح المصدر يذكر أن hypertonic saline وmannitol كلاهما osmotic therapies، مع دعم أقوى واستخدام شائع لـHTS في severe pediatric TBI.
clinicalPearl: Do not treat the recall key as independent verification of the exact regimen.

tts.text: A child with traumatic brain injury has cerebral edema on CT. Which treatment is selected in the source? Option A, mannitol. Option B, three percent sodium chloride infusion. Option C, normal saline infusion.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection, 4th Edition, 1 May 2026

stemEn: According to the recalled question, when should MRI be performed after traumatic brain injury?
explanationAr: مفتاح المصدر C: 5–7 days. المصدر يحيل إلى مرجع عن استخدام MRI في severe pediatric TBI، لكنه لا يعرض تعليلًا كافيًا يجعل هذا التوقيت قاعدة عامة لكل TBI؛ لذلك يحتاج تحقق.
clinicalPearl: MRI timing is context-dependent; retain the exam recall separately from verification.

tts.text: According to the recalled question, when should MRI be performed after traumatic brain injury? Option A, immediately. Option B, one to two days. Option C, five to seven days. Option D, two to three weeks.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection, 4th Edition, 1 May 2026

stemEn: Which measure is considered protective after traumatic brain injury in the recalled question?

options.text: Avoid hypotension to prevent secondary brain injury
Avoid hypertension to prevent intracranial hemorrhage

explanationAr: المصدر يرجّح A لكنه يذكر أن C قد تكون محتملة. أهم ما يدعمه شرح المصدر هو أن hypotension عامل رئيسي في secondary brain injury وأن الحفاظ على perfusion مهم. لذلك السؤال محفوظ كـconflicting بدل تثبيت جواب موثق.
clinicalPearl: Prevent hypotension and hypoxia in pediatric TBI; source wording remains ambiguous.

tts.text: Which measure is considered protective after traumatic brain injury in the recalled question? Option A, avoid hypotension to prevent secondary brain injury. Option B, avoid hypertension to prevent intracranial hemorrhage. Option C, heavy sedation. Option D, hypocarbia below thirty.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection, 4th Edition, 1 May 2026

stemEn: What mechanism explains the short-term intracranial pressure effect of hyperventilation after traumatic brain injury?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار B؛ انخفاض CO2 يسبب cerebral vasoconstriction ويقلل cerebral blood flow وبالتالي يخفض ICP مؤقتًا.
clinicalPearl: Hyperventilation lowers PaCO2 and causes cerebral vasoconstriction.

tts.text: What mechanism explains the short-term intracranial pressure effect of hyperventilation after traumatic brain injury? Option A, increase cerebral blood flow. Option B, cerebral arterial vasoconstriction. Option C, vasodilation.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection, 4th Edition, 1 May 2026

stemEn: After traumatic brain injury with loss of consciousness, which recalled factor increases the risk of later epilepsy?
explanationAr: مفتاح المصدر B: intracranial hemorrhage. السؤال مأخوذ من قسم post-traumatic epilepsy، لكن لم يُجرَ تحقق مستقل من حجم الخطر أو بقية العوامل.
clinicalPearl: Structural intracranial injury is a key risk marker in the recalled item.

tts.text: After traumatic brain injury with loss of consciousness, which recalled factor increases the risk of later epilepsy? Option A, loss of consciousness. Option B, intracranial hemorrhage.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection, 4th Edition, 1 May 2026

stemEn: A child with severe TBI has no spontaneous movement, gag or cough reflex, oculocephalic response, or caloric response after sedation is stopped. What is the next step in the recalled question?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار apnea testing كخطوة لاحقة ضمن تقييم brain death، ولا يسمح بمجرد هذه العلامات بإعلان الوفاة الدماغية مباشرة.
clinicalPearl: Brain-death determination requires a defined protocol; this item preserves the source step only.

tts.text: A child with severe traumatic brain injury has absent brainstem reflexes after sedation is stopped. What is the next step? Option A, EEG. Option B, perform apnea testing. Option C, declare brain death.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection, 4th Edition, 1 May 2026

stemEn: A 4-year-old develops headache and temporal swelling after a minor head injury; skull radiography shows a lytic lesion. How should the diagnosis be reached?
explanationAr: المصدر نفسه يقول إنه لم يجد إجابة لهذا السؤال، ويذكر أن Langerhans cell histiocytosis قد يسبب lytic skull lesion وأن biopsy قد تُستخدم، لكنه يعتبر صياغة الحالة غير مترابطة. لذلك لا تُخترع إجابة.
clinicalPearl: Incomplete/discordant recall: do not force an answer.

tts.text: A four-year-old develops headache and temporal swelling after a minor head injury; skull radiography shows a lytic lesion. How should the diagnosis be reached? Option A, biopsy of the lytic lesion. Option B, MRI brain and spine.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection, 4th Edition, 1 May 2026

stemEn: A stable 5-year-old falls about 0.6 m, has no loss of consciousness and a normal examination. Which imaging option did the source key select for evaluating cervical injury?
explanationAr: المصدر يضع B لكنه يصرّح أن CT غير indicated بالمعلومات المعطاة، ويذكر أن سؤالًا مشابهًا يختار AP/lateral X-rays. لذلك هذا سؤال conflicting ويحتاج مراجعة حديثة قبل النشر.
clinicalPearl: The source key conflicts with its own discussion; preserve the conflict.

tts.text: A stable five-year-old falls about zero point six meters and has a normal examination. Which imaging option did the source key select for evaluating cervical injury? Option A, AP and lateral cervical radiographs. Option B, CT of brain and spine. Option C, neck extension radiograph. Option D, MRI of the spine.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection, 4th Edition, 1 May 2026

stemEn: A child has hemotympanum after a head injury. Which CT-associated diagnosis is most likely?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار basilar skull fracture ويذكر hemotympanum ضمن العلامات الشائعة مع raccoon eyes وBattle sign وCSF leak.
clinicalPearl: Hemotympanum is a classic clue to basilar skull fracture.

tts.text: A child has hemotympanum after a head injury. Which diagnosis is most likely? Option A, basilar skull fracture. Option B, subdural hemorrhage. Option C, epidural hematoma.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection, 4th Edition, 1 May 2026

stemEn: After an RTA, a CT image shows a crescent-shaped intracranial collection. What is the diagnosis?
explanationAr: المصدر يحدد الصورة على أنها crescentic lesion ويعطي Subdural hemorrhage. الصورة الأصلية جزء أساسي من السؤال ولا تُستبدل بصورة مولدة.
clinicalPearl: Image-dependent question; original CT must be linked before publication.

tts.text: After a road traffic accident, a CT image shows a crescent-shaped intracranial collection. What is the diagnosis? Option A, subdural hemorrhage.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection, 4th Edition, 1 May 2026

stemEn: After an RTA with a brief lucid interval, CT shows a lens-shaped intracranial collection. What is the diagnosis?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار epidural hematoma؛ يصفه كـbiconvex/lens-shaped collection مع lucid interval كلاسيكي. الصورة الأصلية لازمة.
clinicalPearl: Lens-shaped CT + lucid interval is the source's EDH pattern.

tts.text: After a road traffic accident with a brief lucid interval, CT shows a lens-shaped intracranial collection. What is the diagnosis? Option A, epidural hematoma. Option B, subdural hematoma. Option C, subarachnoid hemorrhage.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection, 4th Edition, 1 May 2026

stemEn: A post-RTA CT image is described as an epidural hematoma. Which next action is selected by the source?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار immediate evacuation ويشرح أن EDH مع neurologic decompensation يحتاج rapid evacuation. لأن الـstem المختصر لا يوضح كل مؤشرات الجراحة، يبقى التحقق السريري مطلوبًا.
clinicalPearl: Management depends on neurologic status and imaging details; source key retained separately.

tts.text: A post-road-traffic-accident CT image is described as an epidural hematoma. Which next action is selected by the source? Option A, immediate evacuation. Option B, give mannitol.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection, 4th Edition, 1 May 2026

stemEn: An unconscious child after an RTA has a lens-shaped epidural hematoma on CT. What is the next step?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار immediate surgery في الطفل unconscious مع EDH. السؤال image-dependent ويحتاج CT الأصلية.
clinicalPearl: Neurologic deterioration with EDH is an emergency in the source framing.

tts.text: An unconscious child after a road traffic accident has a lens-shaped epidural hematoma on CT. What is the next step? Option A, immediate surgery. Option B, admission and observation.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection, 4th Edition, 1 May 2026

stemEn: A child after an RTA has a lucid interval and a lens-shaped collection on CT. Which diagnosis/management pair is best according to the recall?
explanationAr: المصدر يقول B، أو A إذا وُجد altered mental status أو increased ICP أو focal deficit. لأن الحسم يعتمد على تفاصيل غير كاملة، السؤال conflicting ولا يُنشر كجواب قطعي.
clinicalPearl: The management switch depends on neurologic deterioration and mass effect.

tts.text: A child after a road traffic accident has a lucid interval and a lens-shaped collection on CT. Which diagnosis and management pair is best according to the recall? Option A, epidural hematoma, immediate evacuation. Option B, epidural hematoma, neurosurgery referral. Option C, subdural hemorrhage, immediate evacuation. Option D, subdural hemorrhage, neurosurgery referral.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection, 4th Edition, 1 May 2026

stemEn: A child after an RTA is stable, GCS 15 with no neurologic deficit, but CT shows a lens-shaped epidural hematoma. What is the next step in the source?

options.text: Observe and intervene if deterioration occurs

explanationAr: المصدر يختار urgent neurosurgery consultation، ويضيف أن immediate surgery يصبح مناسبًا إذا ظهرت altered mental status أو increased ICP أو focal findings.
clinicalPearl: Stable EDH still warrants urgent specialist assessment in the source.

tts.text: A child after a road traffic accident is stable, with GCS fifteen and no neurologic deficit, but CT shows an epidural hematoma. What is the next step in the source? Option A, observe and give pain control. Option B, observe and intervene if deterioration occurs. Option C, urgent neurosurgery consultation. Option D, immediate surgery.

stemEn: A 12-year-old has depressed consciousness, labored breathing, withdrawal to pain, and small bilaterally reactive pupils. What is the most likely cause?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار pontine hemorrhage ويذكر أن pontine lesions قد تسبب deep coma مع small/pinpoint reactive pupils بسبب إصابة brainstem pathways.
clinicalPearl: Small reactive pupils with profound depressed consciousness are a pontine clue in this recall.

tts.text: A twelve-year-old has depressed consciousness, labored breathing, withdrawal to pain, and small bilaterally reactive pupils. What is the most likely cause? Option A, pontine hemorrhage. Option B, medulla infarction. Option C, uncal herniation.
